topics.topic: How process-count limits are enforced only for the sandboxed code's tasks
questions: Which passage must change? Setting RLIMIT_NPROC inside the new user namespace does not make its accounting namespace-local: it still accounts tasks for the host real user, including unrelated host tasks, so it cannot be the stated outer bound over only the code's tasks.

quotes: the outer process bound is the setrlimit limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1, set by the runner inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code, soft and hard alike (every limit is set soft and hard to the same value; bubblewrap is started without any capability option, so the code holds none and cannot raise a limit), a runner that cannot set it exiting before it loads the code so the execution is crashed — the one is the task bubblewrap's init would be, and with the runner as the namespace's init it is the margin that keeps the outer bound above the audit hook's exact count; set by the parent, that limit would count every process of the user on the host and bubblewrap could not create its namespace (EAGAIN) — process_count itself being enforced by the runner's audit hook

process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks.
judgement.why: The text explicitly specifies both the outer setrlimit mechanism and the audit-hook enforcement that counts only the code's tasks; the topic disputes that mechanism's real-world validity rather than identifying two contradictory passages.

topics.topic: How the trap file descriptor is passed through bubblewrap to the sandboxed child
questions: The trap channel must reach the sandboxed child, but subprocess pass_fds preserves it only into bubblewrap; bubblewrap must explicitly preserve it for the child, using its --preserve-fds option. Must the instruction denying that option change, or must another supported descriptor-passing mechanism be specified?

quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
judgement.why: This asks the same descriptor-preservation question as P4, and the quoted passage has not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: How bubblewrap preserves the inherited trap-channel descriptor for the runner without a descriptor-preservation option
quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
precedent.why: The text explicitly requires pass_fds inheritance into bubblewrap and requires bubblewrap to keep the descriptors open for its child.

topics.topic: Definition of mapped-node readiness for advance_run
questions: Must readiness mean only that every input port holds its value, or must a mapped node also have at least one unconcluded, non-waiting element that can execute?

judgement.why: This asks the same mapped-node readiness question as P3, and the quoted passage and relevant change have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Whether input availability alone determines node readiness when mapped elements are waiting
quotes: A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element that has no concluded record and does not wait — an operation element that waits is not reached again here — before the next node is selected; an operation element waits when operation_element_conclusion answers ElementWaiting, whether or not it has a NodeExecution (one waiting for the owner's approval has none), and a node none of whose elements without a concluded record can execute is not ready, so the next ready node is selected among the others;
precedent.why: The text expressly classifies a node with no executable unconcluded elements as not ready, even if its inputs are present.
